# The Android app (mobile/): the web build bundled inside a Capacitor shell, so Ward works with
# the internet off. Run by hand from the Actions tab (APK kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag,
# which attaches Ward-android.apk to that GitHub Release. The name never changes, so
# releases/latest/download/Ward-android.apk always points at the newest one.
#
# Signing: the keystore lives only in repository secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64,
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD). Without them a hand run
# builds a debug-signed APK instead (installable, but updates must be signed the same way),
# and a tag run fails.
name: Android app

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm sync
        working-directory: mobile
      - name: Keystore
        id: keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12"
            echo "path=$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/* ]]; then
            echo "::error::A release needs the signing secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the rest)."
            exit 1
          else
            echo "::warning::No signing secrets, so this is a debug build."
          fi
      - name: Build
        working-directory: mobile/android
        env:
          WARD_KEYSTORE: ${{ steps.keystore.outputs.path }}
          WARD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          WARD_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          WARD_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../release
          if [ -n "$WARD_KEYSTORE" ]; then
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleRelease
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          else
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          fi
          "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs ../../release/Ward-android.apk | head -3
      # Ward Lite reads on the phone only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model are in the APK;
      # without them Ward quietly falls back to word lists alone.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the APK
        run: |
          unzip -l release/Ward-android.apk | awk '$1 > 0 { print $4 }' > apk-files.txt
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            grep -qxF "assets/public/$f" apk-files.txt || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the APK"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the APK"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: release/Ward-android.apk
          retention-days: 14
      # The emulator's "Give Ward to a friend" check needs a debug build: only it has the check
      # receiver. A run without signing secrets has just built one, so this costs nothing there.
      - name: Debug build for the give-a-friend check
        working-directory: mobile/android
        run: |
          [ -f app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ] || ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
          mkdir -p ../../give && cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../give/Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
          path: give/Ward-debug.apk
          retention-days: 3

  # Install the APK on an emulator, open it, and keep a screenshot and the log: Ward starts,
  # shows onboarding from the bundle with no network, and doesn't crash. Then "Give Ward to a
  # friend": the copy it shares is exactly the installed APK and installs on a wiped phone.
  launch:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            packages/engine/fixtures
            mobile/ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            adb install -r Ward-android.apk
            adb shell svc wifi disable; adb shell svc data disable
            adb logcat -c
            adb shell am start -W -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 30
            adb exec-out screencap -p > launch.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            # Share to Ward: hand it a WhatsApp export the way WhatsApp's share sheet does.
            adb push packages/engine/fixtures/pileon-roman-urdu.txt "/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt"
            adb shell chmod 644 "'/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'"
            adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain --eu android.intent.extra.STREAM "'file:///data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'" -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 10
            adb exec-out screencap -p > share.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            ! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" logcat.txt
            # Give Ward to a friend: copy the installed APK as the share sheet would, check it's
            # byte for byte the same, then install that copy on a wiped "friend's phone".
            bash mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ward-android-launch
          path: |
            launch.png
            share.png
            logcat.txt
            give-logcat.txt
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: [build, launch]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: Ward-android.apk
# Typecheck and test every package, and build the web app, on every push. The build fails if
# Ward Lite (ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model) is missing from its output.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm -r typecheck
      # The root test script: every package's tests plus the loose test files, so CI never drifts from it.
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
# Desktop installers for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. Run by hand from
# the Actions tab (kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag, which publishes them on the Release.
# Each packaged app is launched once (WARD_SMOKE, which also opens Ward Lite) before it's kept.
# Unsigned for now.
# Gemma's model is never in the installer (Ward downloads it on request); llama.cpp's binaries
# for the runner's platform are, minus CUDA (Vulkan and CPU cover Windows and Linux).
name: Desktop installers

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            name: mac-arm64
            target: --mac dmg --arm64
            app: release/mac-arm64/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward
            resources: release/mac-arm64/Ward.app/Contents/Resources
          - os: macos-15-intel
            name: mac-x64
            target: --mac dmg --x64
            app: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward
            resources: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/Resources
          - os: windows-latest
            name: windows-x64
            target: --win nsis --x64
            app: release/win-unpacked/Ward.exe
            resources: release/win-unpacked/resources
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            name: linux-x64
            target: --linux AppImage --x64
            app: release/linux-unpacked/ward
            resources: release/linux-unpacked/resources
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm exec electron-builder ${{ matrix.target }} --publish never
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
      # Ward Lite reads in the app only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model were packaged; the
      # launch test below then opens the model with that runtime inside the app's own page.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            [ -s "${{ matrix.resources }}/web/$f" ] || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the packaged app"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the app"
      - name: Launch test
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: WARD_SMOKE=1 "${{ matrix.app }}"
      - name: Launch test (virtual display)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq xvfb > /dev/null
          WARD_SMOKE=1 xvfb-run -a "${{ matrix.app }}" --no-sandbox
      # The Gemma built into Ward (node-llama-cpp's prebuilt llama.cpp) must load in the packaged
      # app, with lab mode both off and on. Required since it first loaded on all four platforms.
      - name: Built-in Gemma and lab mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ]; then
            WARD_SMOKE=llama xvfb-run -a "${{ matrix.app }}" --no-sandbox --lab
          else
            WARD_SMOKE=llama "${{ matrix.app }}" --lab
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: |
            release/*.dmg
            release/*.exe
            release/*.AppImage
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: installers/*
          generate_release_notes: true

# Typecheck and test every package, and build the web app, on every push. The build fails if
# Ward Lite (ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model) is missing from its output.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm -r typecheck
      # The root test script: every package's tests plus the loose test files, so CI never drifts from it.
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
# Desktop installers for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. Run by hand from
# the Actions tab (kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag, which publishes them on the Release.
# Each packaged app is launched once (WARD_SMOKE, which also opens Ward Lite) before it's kept.
# Unsigned for now.
# Gemma's model is never in the installer (Ward downloads it on request); llama.cpp's binaries
# for the runner's platform are, minus CUDA (Vulkan and CPU cover Windows and Linux).
name: Desktop installers

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            name: mac-arm64
            target: --mac dmg --arm64
            app: release/mac-arm64/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward
            resources: release/mac-arm64/Ward.app/Contents/Resources
          - os: macos-15-intel
            name: mac-x64
            target: --mac dmg --x64
            app: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward
            resources: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/Resources
          - os: windows-latest
            name: windows-x64
            target: --win nsis --x64
            app: release/win-unpacked/Ward.exe
            resources: release/win-unpacked/resources
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            name: linux-x64
            target: --linux AppImage --x64
            app: release/linux-unpacked/ward
            resources: release/linux-unpacked/resources
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm exec electron-builder ${{ matrix.target }} --publish never
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
      # Ward Lite reads in the app only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model were packaged; the
      # launch test below then opens the model with that runtime inside the app's own page.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            [ -s "${{ matrix.resources }}/web/$f" ] || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the packaged app"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the app"
      - name: Launch test
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: WARD_SMOKE=1 "${{ matrix.app }}"
      - name: Launch test (virtual display)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq xvfb > /dev/null
          WARD_SMOKE=1 xvfb-run -a "${{ matrix.app }}" --no-sandbox
      # The Gemma built into Ward (node-llama-cpp's prebuilt llama.cpp) must load in the packaged
      # app, with lab mode both off and on. Required since it first loaded on all four platforms.
      - name: Built-in Gemma and lab mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ]; then
            WARD_SMOKE=llama xvfb-run -a "${{ matrix.app }}" --no-sandbox --lab
          else
            WARD_SMOKE=llama "${{ matrix.app }}" --lab
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: |
            release/*.dmg
            release/*.exe
            release/*.AppImage
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: installers/*
          generate_release_notes: true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# "Give Ward to a friend" on the emulator (.github/workflows/android.yml, launch job).
#
# 1. Installs the debug APK (only debug builds have the check receiver) and makes the same copy
#    the share sheet gets, through GiveCheckReceiver.
# 2. Checks the copy is byte for byte the installed APK: the hash of the installed file, the
#    copy on disk, the copy read back through the FileProvider, and the plugin's own hash must
#    all match, the provider must report the APK MIME type, and the plugin's certificate
#    fingerprint must match apksigner's.
# 3. Plays the friend: pulls the copy off the "phone", uninstalls Ward, installs the copy and
#    opens it.
#
# What this can't do: a real Bluetooth or Quick Share transfer between two phones. The share
# sheet hands that to the system, which an emulator can't exercise.
#
# Usage: mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
set -euo pipefail

APK="${1:-Ward-debug.apk}"
PKG=org.ward.app
fail() { echo "::error::give-check: $*"; adb logcat -d > give-logcat.txt || true; exit 1; }

adb uninstall "$PKG" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
adb install "$APK"
adb shell am start -W -n "$PKG/.MainActivity" > /dev/null
adb logcat -c
adb shell am broadcast -n "$PKG/.GiveCheckReceiver"

line=""
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  line=$(adb logcat -d -s WardGive:I | grep -m1 GIVE_CHECK || true)
  [ -n "$line" ] && break
  sleep 1
done
echo "$line"
case "$line" in *"GIVE_CHECK ok"*) ;; *) fail "the copy wasn't made" ;; esac

field() { echo "$line" | tr ' ' '\n' | tr -d '\r' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"; }
norm() { tr -d ' :\r' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'; }

installed_path=$(adb shell pm path "$PKG" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^package://p' | head -1)
installed=$(adb shell sha256sum "$installed_path" | awk '{print $1}')
name=$(field file)
on_disk=$(adb shell run-as "$PKG" sha256sum "cache/give/$name" | awk '{print $1}')
# build-tools label it "Signer #1", "V2 Signer:" or "Signer (minSdkVersion=…)"; print what we
# got so a format change is easy to see.
apksigner_out=$("$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs "$APK" 2>/dev/null)
echo "$apksigner_out" | grep -i "sha-256" || true
signer=$(echo "$apksigner_out" | sed -n 's/^.*[Ss]igner.*certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' | head -1 | norm)

echo "installed  $installed ($installed_path)"
echo "plugin     $(field apk)"
echo "copy       $(field copy)"
echo "on disk    $on_disk (cache/give/$name)"
echo "provider   $(field provider) ($(field type))"
echo "cert       $(field cert)"
echo "apksigner  $signer"

[ -n "$installed" ] || fail "couldn't hash the installed APK"
[[ "$name" == Ward-*.apk ]] || fail "unexpected file name $name"
[ "$(field split)" = "false" ] || fail "the emulator install is split"
[ "$(field apk)" = "$installed" ] || fail "plugin hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field copy)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$on_disk" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy on disk differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field provider)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy read through the FileProvider differs"
[ "$(field type)" = "application/vnd.android.package-archive" ] || fail "FileProvider gives type $(field type)"
[ -n "$signer" ] && [ "$(field cert | norm)" = "$signer" ] || fail "certificate fingerprint differs from apksigner's"

# The friend's phone: the copy, and only the copy, installs and opens.
adb exec-out run-as "$PKG" cat "cache/give/$name" > friend.apk
[ "$(sha256sum friend.apk | awk '{print $1}')" = "$installed" ] || fail "pulled copy differs"
adb uninstall "$PKG"
adb install friend.apk
adb logcat -c
adb shell am start -W -n "$PKG/.MainActivity"
sleep 8
adb logcat -d > give-logcat.txt
adb shell pidof "$PKG" > /dev/null || fail "the friend's copy didn't stay open"
! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" give-logcat.txt || fail "the friend's copy crashed"
echo "give-check: the copy matches the installed APK and installs on a fresh phone"

case "$line" in *"GIVE_CHECK ok"*) ;; *) fail "the copy wasn't made" ;; esac

field() { echo "$line" | tr ' ' '\n' | tr -d '\r' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"; }
norm() { tr -d ' :\r' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'; }

installed_path=$(adb shell pm path "$PKG" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^package://p' | head -1)
installed=$(adb shell sha256sum "$installed_path" | awk '{print $1}')
name=$(field file)
on_disk=$(adb shell run-as "$PKG" sha256sum "cache/give/$name" | awk '{print $1}')
# build-tools label it "Signer #1", "V2 Signer:" or "Signer (minSdkVersion=…)"; print what we
# got so a format change is easy to see.
apksigner_out=$("$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs "$APK" 2>/dev/null)
echo "$apksigner_out" | grep -i "sha-256" || true
signer=$(echo "$apksigner_out" | sed -n 's/^.*[Ss]igner.*certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' | head -1 | norm)

echo "installed  $installed ($installed_path)"
echo "plugin     $(field apk)"
echo "copy       $(field copy)"
echo "on disk    $on_disk (cache/give/$name)"
echo "provider   $(field provider) ($(field type))"
echo "cert       $(field cert)"
echo "apksigner  $signer"

[ -n "$installed" ] || fail "couldn't hash the installed APK"
[[ "$name" == Ward-*.apk ]] || fail "unexpected file name $name"
[ "$(field split)" = "false" ] || fail "the emulator install is split"
[ "$(field apk)" = "$installed" ] || fail "plugin hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field copy)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$on_disk" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy on disk differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field provider)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy read through the FileProvider differs"
[ "$(field type)" = "application/vnd.android.package-archive" ] || fail "FileProvider gives type $(field type)"
[ -n "$signer" ] && [ "$(field cert | norm)" = "$signer" ] || fail "certificate fingerprint differs from apksigner's"

# The friend's phone: the copy, and only the copy, installs and opens.
adb exec-out run-as "$PKG" cat "cache/give/$name" > friend.apk
[ "$(sha256sum friend.apk | awk '{print $1}')" = "$installed" ] || fail "pulled copy differs"
adb uninstall "$PKG"
adb install friend.apk
adb logcat -c
adb shell am start -W -n "$PKG/.MainActivity"
sleep 8
adb logcat -d > give-logcat.txt
adb shell pidof "$PKG" > /dev/null || fail "the friend's copy didn't stay open"
! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" give-logcat.txt || fail "the friend's copy crashed"
echo "give-check: the copy matches the installed APK and installs on a fresh phone"

content.content:
Ward

A guardian that lives on a child's own device. It spots cyberbullying in English, Roman Urdu,
Hinglish and Bangla, keeps the evidence, coaches the next step, and trains kids to bounce back.
Open-weight Gemma, running locally. No server and no account: a child's messages never go to us or to any AI company.

No release yet. Until the first version is published, build Ward from source.

The bully is the ghost haunting the chat. Ward is the ghost on your side. Before you put Ward in front of a child, read the draft [safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md): what Ward will never do, what hasn't been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet, and [how to raise a concern](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#10-raising-a-concern-about-the-project-itself). ## What this is, and what it isn't Ward is a response to World Solve problem [WS05937](https://www.worldsolve.org/index.php?view=problem&id=5937): *Building effective interventions for cyberbullying harming children by 2030*, built for the DEV Hacktoberfest pnpm install node apps/web/scripts/copy-ort.mjs # Ward Lite's offline runtime (not in git); rerun after updating packages ollama pull gemma4:e4b # the close read; Ward still works without it pnpm dev # http://localhost:5199 pnpm test # every package, plus the viewer, corrections and red-team leak check pnpm eval # the scorecard (also needs: ollama pull shieldgemma:2b) ``` Skip the `copy-ort` step and the app still runs, but without Ward Lite, in the dev server and in every build below: where Gemma isn't set up, Ward reads with the word lists alone. - **Desktop:** `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop start`. No Ollama? Me → "Gemma inside Ward" downloads Gemma 4 once (4.6 GB) and runs it through llama.cpp inside the app. `--lab` (or the switch in Me) makes Ward forget everything on close, for shared school computers. `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop dist` builds an installer for your own computer into `release/`. GitHub Actions (`desktop.yml`) builds and launch-tests installers for macOS, Windows and Linux when run by hand; none has been published as a release yet. - **Android:** `mobile/` is a Capacitor shell with the app bundled inside and a small native plugin for Share to Ward. `pnpm --filter @ward/web build && pnpm --filter @ward/mobile apk` builds a debug APK (needs the Android SDK and JDK 21). `android.yml` builds it and launch-tests it on an emulator with Wi-Fi off. Cloud backup is off, so the vault never leaves the phone. - **Phone + family computer:** start Ollama on the computer with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, then put `http://:11434` in Ward's Me screen on the phone. The phone then sends the chats it checks to that computer over your home network, unencrypted, so only do this on a network you trust. `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` lets anyone on that network use the computer's Ollama: never set it on school or public Wi-Fi. ### Opening an unsigned build Ward's installers aren't signed yet, so the first time you open one your computer warns you. - **macOS 15 and later:** open Ward once and click Done on the warning. Then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and click **Open Anyway** next to the line about Ward. Confirm with your password, and Ward opens. (Right-click → Open no longer skips the check on macOS 15.) If there's no Open Anyway button, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Ward.app` in Terminal, then open Ward. - **Windows:** if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - **Linux:** make the AppImage runnable with `chmod +x Ward-linux.AppImage`, then open it. ## How it's built ``` packages/engine parser, slang packs, pattern engine, Gemma and ShieldGemma judges, the ward.report/v2 builder; unit-tested packages/lessons the Resilience Path as plain data, with content tests apps/web React 19, Vite, Tailwind 4, Motion, Phosphor icons desktop Electron, served from app://ward (one of Ollama's allowed origins) mobile Capacitor Android with the ShareIn and Give Ward plugins apps/discord the Discord bot (discord.js), same engine and Ward Lite in Node eval datasets, baselines and the scorecard docs PLAN, HARMS, SAFEGUARDING, REPORT, REDTEAM, ROADMAP, DPG ``` The drop zone's travelling rim light is adapted from the idea in cult-ui's Halo Dropzone on 21st.dev. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. ## Help wanted If you work at a child helpline, a school, or with young people in Pakistan, India or f299322 README: building from source needs the copy-ort step for Ward Lite 9d4be8c README: claims match the code and the scorecard 7f9bfbc Docs: Phase 4 complete, Phase 5 progress, Discord, and the retrained Ward Lite DPG.md GOVERNANCE.md HARMS.md PHASES.md PLAN.md REDTEAM.md REPORT.md ROADMAP.md SAFEGUARDING.md

Before you put Ward in front of a child, read the draft [safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md): what Ward will never do, what hasn't been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet, and [how to raise a concern](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#10-raising-a-concern-about-the-project-itself). ## What this is, and what it isn't Ward is a response to World Solve problem [WS05937](https://www.worldsolve.org/index.php?view=problem&id=5937): *Building effective interventions for cyberbullying harming children by 2030*, built for the DEV Hacktoberfest pnpm install node apps/web/scripts/copy-ort.mjs # Ward Lite's offline runtime (not in git); rerun after updating packages ollama pull gemma4:e4b # the close read; Ward still works without it pnpm dev # http://localhost:5199 pnpm test # every package, plus the viewer, corrections and red-team leak check pnpm eval # the scorecard (also needs: ollama pull shieldgemma:2b) ``` Skip the `copy-ort` step and the app still runs, but without Ward Lite, in the dev server and in every build below: where Gemma isn't set up, Ward reads with the word lists alone. - **Desktop:** `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop start`. No Ollama? Me → "Gemma inside Ward" downloads Gemma 4 once (4.6 GB) and runs it through llama.cpp inside the app. `--lab` (or the switch in Me) makes Ward forget everything on close, for shared school computers. `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop dist` builds an installer for your own computer into `release/`. GitHub Actions (`desktop.yml`) builds and launch-tests installers for macOS, Windows and Linux when run by hand; none has been published as a release yet. - **Android:** `mobile/` is a Capacitor shell with the app bundled inside and a small native plugin for Share to Ward. `pnpm --filter @ward/web build && pnpm --filter @ward/mobile apk` builds a debug APK (needs the Android SDK and JDK 21). `android.yml` builds it and launch-tests it on an emulator with Wi-Fi off. Cloud backup is off, so the vault never leaves the phone. - **Phone + family computer:** start Ollama on the computer with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, then put `http://:11434` in Ward's Me screen on the phone. The phone then sends the chats it checks to that computer over your home network, unencrypted, so only do this on a network you trust. `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` lets anyone on that network use the computer's Ollama: never set it on school or public Wi-Fi. ### Opening an unsigned build Ward's installers aren't signed yet, so the first time you open one your computer warns you. - **macOS 15 and later:** open Ward once and click Done on the warning. Then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and click **Open Anyway** next to the line about Ward. Confirm with your password, and Ward opens. (Right-click → Open no longer skips the check on macOS 15.) If there's no Open Anyway button, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Ward.app` in Terminal, then open Ward. - **Windows:** if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - **Linux:** make the AppImage runnable with `chmod +x Ward-linux.AppImage`, then open it. ## How it's built ``` packages/engine parser, slang packs, pattern engine, Gemma and ShieldGemma judges, the ward.report/v2 builder; unit-tested packages/lessons the Resilience Path as plain data, with content tests apps/web React 19, Vite, Tailwind 4, Motion, Phosphor icons desktop Electron, served from app://ward (one of Ollama's allowed origins) mobile Capacitor Android with the ShareIn and Give Ward plugins apps/discord the Discord bot (discord.js), same engine and Ward Lite in Node eval datasets, baselines and the scorecard docs PLAN, HARMS, SAFEGUARDING, REPORT, REDTEAM, ROADMAP, DPG ``` The drop zone's travelling rim light is adapted from the idea in cult-ui's Halo Dropzone on 21st.dev. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. ## Help wanted If you work at a child helpline, a school, or with young people in Pakistan, India or f299322 README: building from source needs the copy-ort step for Ward Lite 9d4be8c README: claims match the code and the scorecard 7f9bfbc Docs: Phase 4 complete, Phase 5 progress, Discord, and the retrained Ward Lite DPG.md GOVERNANCE.md HARMS.md PHASES.md PLAN.md REDTEAM.md REPORT.md ROADMAP.md SAFEGUARDING.md

# The Android app (mobile/): the web build bundled inside a Capacitor shell, so Ward works with
# the internet off. Two APKs (mobile/android/app/build.gradle):
#   Ward-android.apk        "lite", the default: no native code, installs on any phone, 32-bit too
#   Ward-android-gemma.apk  adds on-phone Gemma 4 E2B (LiteRT-LM), arm64 phones only
# Run by hand from the Actions tab (APKs kept 14 days). release.yml calls this on a v* tag and
# publishes the APKs; the names never change.
#
# Signing: the keystore lives only in repository secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64,
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; docs/RELEASING.md). Without
# them a hand run builds debug APKs instead (app id org.ward.app.debug, so they install beside a
# release rather than over it), and a release run fails.
name: Android app

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      release:
        description: Build signed release APKs, versioned from the tag
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@fc06bc1257f339d1d5d8b3a19a8cae5388b55320 # v4.4.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@cf277c60eb25467037889841efdb72551f06f6c3 # v4.9.1
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm sync
        working-directory: mobile
      - name: Keystore
        id: keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          RELEASE: ${{ inputs.release }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12"
            echo "path=$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$RELEASE" = true ]; then
            echo "::error::A release needs the signing secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the rest, docs/RELEASING.md)."
            exit 1
          else
            echo "::warning::No signing secrets, so these are debug builds."
          fi
      - name: Build
        working-directory: mobile/android
        env:
          WARD_KEYSTORE: ${{ steps.keystore.outputs.path }}
          WARD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          WARD_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          WARD_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # The tag (v0.1.0) sets versionName and versionCode; a hand run is 0.0.0-dev.
          WARD_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' && github.ref_name || '' }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../release
          if [ -n "$WARD_KEYSTORE" ]; then type=release; else type=debug; fi
          ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleLite${type^} assembleGemma${type^}
          cp app/build/outputs/apk/lite/$type/app-lite-$type.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          cp app/build/outputs/apk/gemma/$type/app-gemma-$type.apk ../../release/Ward-android-gemma.apk
          tools="$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)"
          for apk in ../../release/*.apk; do
            echo "== $(basename "$apk"): $("$tools"/aapt2 dump badging "$apk" | head -1)"
            "$tools"/apksigner verify --print-certs "$apk" | grep -i "SHA-256"
          done
      # Lite must have no native code at all: that is what lets it install on 32-bit and any other
      # ABI. Gemma carries LiteRT-LM's libraries for arm64 and nothing else.
      - name: Native libraries
        run: |
          for apk in Ward-android Ward-android-gemma; do
            unzip -l release/$apk.apk | awk '{ print $4 }' | grep '^lib/' | sort > $apk-libs.txt || true
            echo "== $apk.apk native libraries:"; cat $apk-libs.txt
          done
          [ ! -s Ward-android-libs.txt ] || { echo "::error::The lite APK has native libraries, so it won't install on every phone"; exit 1; }
          diff -u - Ward-android-gemma-libs.txt <<'EOF' || { echo "::error::The gemma APK's native libraries changed (expected above, got below)"; exit 1; }
          lib/arm64-v8a/liblitertlm_jni.so
          EOF
      # Ward Lite reads on the phone only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model are in the APK;
      # without them Ward quietly falls back to word lists alone.
      - name: Ward Lite is in both APKs
        run: |
          for apk in release/*.apk; do
            unzip -l "$apk" | awk '$1 > 0 { print $4 }' > apk-files.txt
            for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
              grep -qxF "assets/public/$f" apk-files.txt || { echo "::error::$f is missing from $apk"; exit 1; }
            done
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in both APKs"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: release/*.apk
          retention-days: 14
      # The emulator's "Give Ward to a friend" check needs a debug build: only it has the check
      # receiver. A run without signing secrets has just built one, so this costs nothing there.
      - name: Debug build for the give-a-friend check
        working-directory: mobile/android
        run: |
          [ -f app/build/outputs/apk/lite/debug/app-lite-debug.apk ] || ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleLiteDebug
          mkdir -p ../../give && cp app/build/outputs/apk/lite/debug/app-lite-debug.apk ../../give/Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
          path: give/Ward-debug.apk
          retention-days: 3

  # Install the lite APK on an emulator, open it, and keep a screenshot and the log: Ward starts,
  # shows onboarding from the bundle with no network, and doesn't crash. Then "Give Ward to a
  # friend": the copy it shares is exactly the installed APK and installs on a wiped phone.
  # (The emulator is x86_64, so the arm64-only gemma APK can't be launched here.)
  launch:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            packages/engine/fixtures
            mobile/ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            bash mobile/ci/launch-check.sh Ward-android.apk
            bash mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ward-android-launch
          path: |
            launch.png
            share.png
            logcat.txt
            give-logcat.txt
          retention-days: 14

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# The Android app (mobile/): the web build bundled inside a Capacitor shell, so Ward works with
# the internet off. Run by hand from the Actions tab (APK kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag,
# which attaches Ward-android.apk to that GitHub Release. The name never changes, so
# releases/latest/download/Ward-android.apk always points at the newest one.
#
# Signing: the keystore lives only in repository secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64,
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD). Without them a hand run
# builds a debug-signed APK instead (installable, but updates must be signed the same way),
# and a tag run fails.
name: Android app

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm sync
        working-directory: mobile
      - name: Keystore
        id: keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12"
            echo "path=$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/* ]]; then
            echo "::error::A release needs the signing secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the rest)."
            exit 1
          else
            echo "::warning::No signing secrets, so this is a debug build."
          fi
      - name: Build
        working-directory: mobile/android
        env:
          WARD_KEYSTORE: ${{ steps.keystore.outputs.path }}
          WARD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          WARD_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          WARD_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../release
          if [ -n "$WARD_KEYSTORE" ]; then
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleRelease
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          else
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          fi
          "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs ../../release/Ward-android.apk | head -3
      # Ward Lite reads on the phone only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model are in the APK;
      # without them Ward quietly falls back to word lists alone.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the APK
        run: |
          unzip -l release/Ward-android.apk | awk '$1 > 0 { print $4 }' > apk-files.txt
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            grep -qxF "assets/public/$f" apk-files.txt || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the APK"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the APK"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: release/Ward-android.apk
          retention-days: 14
      # The emulator's "Give Ward to a friend" check needs a debug build: only it has the check
      # receiver. A run without signing secrets has just built one, so this costs nothing there.
      - name: Debug build for the give-a-friend check
        working-directory: mobile/android
        run: |
          [ -f app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ] || ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
          mkdir -p ../../give && cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../give/Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
          path: give/Ward-debug.apk
          retention-days: 3

  # Install the APK on an emulator, open it, and keep a screenshot and the log: Ward starts,
  # shows onboarding from the bundle with no network, and doesn't crash. Then "Give Ward to a
  # friend": the copy it shares is exactly the installed APK and installs on a wiped phone.
  launch:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            packages/engine/fixtures
            mobile/ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            adb install -r Ward-android.apk
            adb shell svc wifi disable; adb shell svc data disable
            adb logcat -c
            adb shell am start -W -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 30
            adb exec-out screencap -p > launch.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            # Share to Ward: hand it a WhatsApp export the way WhatsApp's share sheet does.
            adb push packages/engine/fixtures/pileon-roman-urdu.txt "/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt"
            adb shell chmod 644 "'/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'"
            adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain --eu android.intent.extra.STREAM "'file:///data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'" -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 10
            adb exec-out screencap -p > share.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            ! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" logcat.txt
            # Give Ward to a friend: copy the installed APK as the share sheet would, check it's
            # byte for byte the same, then install that copy on a wiped "friend's phone".
            bash mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ward-android-launch
          path: |
            launch.png
            share.png
            logcat.txt
            give-logcat.txt
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: [build, launch]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: Ward-android.apk

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Ward starts on the emulator (.github/workflows/android.yml, launch job): installs the APK, opens
# it with Wi-Fi and data off, then shares a WhatsApp export to it the way WhatsApp's share sheet
# does. Keeps launch.png, share.png and logcat.txt, and fails if Ward crashes or doesn't stay open.
#
# The package is read from the APK: org.ward.app for a release build, org.ward.app.debug for a
# debug one. The activity class is org.ward.app.MainActivity either way.
#
# Usage: mobile/ci/launch-check.sh Ward-android.apk
set -euo pipefail

APK="${1:-Ward-android.apk}"
tools="$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)"
PKG=$("$tools"/aapt2 dump packagename "$APK")
MAIN="$PKG/org.ward.app.MainActivity"
fail() { echo "::error::launch-check: $*"; adb logcat -d > logcat.txt || true; exit 1; }
crashed() { grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" logcat.txt; }

echo "launch-check: $APK is $PKG"
adb install -r "$APK"
adb shell svc wifi disable
adb shell svc data disable
adb logcat -c
adb shell am start -W -n "$MAIN"
sleep 30
adb exec-out screencap -p > launch.png
adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
adb shell pidof "$PKG" > /dev/null || fail "Ward didn't stay open"

# Share to Ward: hand it a WhatsApp export the way WhatsApp's share sheet does.
adb push packages/engine/fixtures/pileon-roman-urdu.txt "/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt"
adb shell chmod 644 "'/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'"
adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain --eu android.intent.extra.STREAM "'file:///data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'" -n "$MAIN"
sleep 10
adb exec-out screencap -p > share.png
adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
adb shell pidof "$PKG" > /dev/null || fail "Ward didn't stay open after a share"
! crashed || fail "Ward crashed"
echo "launch-check: Ward opened offline and took a shared chat without crashing"
EOF
chmod +x mobile/ci/launch-check.sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='mobile/ci/give-check.sh'

''')

s=s.replace('adb shell am broadcast -n "$PKG/.GiveCheckReceiver"','adb shell am broadcast -n "$PKG/org.ward.app.GiveCheckReceiver"')

input.content:
# A release, from a v* tag the owner pushes (docs/RELEASING.md). Builds the signed Android APKs
# (android.yml, including the emulator launch test) and the desktop installers (desktop.yml,
# each launch-tested), then publishes them as a GitHub prerelease with SHA256SUMS and the
# signing certificate's SHA-256 in the release notes: the fingerprint Ward shows under "Give
# Ward to a friend". Fails before building anything if a signing secret is missing.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Signing secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          missing=""
          for s in ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            [ -n "${!s}" ] || missing="$missing $s"
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::error::Can't release without the signing secrets. Missing:$missing. Add them with gh secret set (docs/RELEASING.md), then delete and push the tag again."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All four signing secrets are set."
      - name: Tag is a version
        run: |
          [[ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]] || {
            echo "::error::The tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME isn't a version like v0.1.0 or v0.1.0-rc.1"; exit 1; }

  android:
    needs: check
    uses: ./.github/workflows/android.yml
    with:
      release: true
    secrets: inherit

  desktop:
    needs: check
    uses: ./.github/workflows/desktop.yml

  publish:
    needs: [android, desktop]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: files
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          pattern: ward-desktop-*
          path: files
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Check the files
        id: cert
        working-directory: files
        run: |
          expected="Ward-android-gemma.apk Ward-android.apk Ward-linux.AppImage Ward-mac-arm64.dmg Ward-mac-x64.dmg Ward-windows-setup.exe"
          [ "$(ls | sort | xargs)" = "$expected" ] || { echo "::error::Expected $expected, got $(ls | xargs)"; exit 1; }
          tools="$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)"
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          certs=""
          for apk in Ward-android.apk Ward-android-gemma.apk; do
            out=$("$tools"/apksigner verify --print-certs "$apk")
            echo "$out"
            ! echo "$out" | grep -q "CN=Android Debug" || { echo "::error::$apk is signed with a debug key"; exit 1; }
            certs="$certs $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/^.*[Ss]igner.*certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' | head -1)"
            name=$("$tools"/aapt2 dump badging "$apk" | sed -n "s/.*versionName='\([^']*\)'.*/\1/p")
            case "$name" in "$version"|"$version-gemma") ;; *) echo "::error::$apk is version $name, the tag says $version"; exit 1 ;; esac
          done
          set -- $certs
          [ -n "$1" ] && [ "$1" = "$2" ] || { echo "::error::The two APKs aren't signed with the same certificate ($certs)"; exit 1; }
          echo "sha256=$1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          sha256sum * > ../SHA256SUMS
          cat ../SHA256SUMS
      - name: Publish the prerelease
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CERT: ${{ steps.cert.outputs.sha256 }}
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          groups=$(echo "$CERT" | tr 'a-f' 'A-F' | fold -w4 | xargs)
          run="$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          cat > notes.md <<EOF
          **A preview.** Before you put Ward in front of a child, read the [safeguarding policy](https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/blob/$GITHUB_REF_NAME/docs/SAFEGUARDING.md): parts of Ward haven't been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet.

          ### Which file?

          | File | For |
          |---|---|
          | \`Ward-android.apk\` | Android 7 and later, any phone, 32-bit ones included. Ward Lite reads chats on the phone. Start here. |
          | \`Ward-android-gemma.apk\` | Android phones with a 64-bit (arm64) chip. Adds the choice to download Gemma 4 E2B (2 GB), which helps write, on phones with 6 GB of RAM or more. |
          | \`Ward-mac-arm64.dmg\` | Macs with Apple Silicon |
          | \`Ward-mac-x64.dmg\` | Intel Macs |
          | \`Ward-windows-setup.exe\` | Windows, 64-bit |
          | \`Ward-linux.AppImage\` | Linux, 64-bit |

          Both APKs are the same app signed with the same key, so either can replace the other. The desktop installers aren't signed yet: see [opening an unsigned build](https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/blob/$GITHUB_REF_NAME/README.md#opening-an-unsigned-build).

          ### Is it the real Ward?

          Ward's signing certificate (SHA-256). Ward shows the same boxes under "Give Ward to a friend"; every one should match.

          \`\`\`
          $groups
          \`\`\`

          On a computer: \`apksigner verify --print-certs Ward-android.apk\` should print \`$CERT\`.

          Every file's SHA-256 is in \`SHA256SUMS\`. Check a download with \`sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS\` (Linux), \`shasum -a 256 <file>\` (macOS) or \`Get-FileHash <file>\` (Windows PowerShell), and compare with its line.

          Built by [this workflow run]($run) from commit \`$GITHUB_SHA\`.
          EOF
          gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" files/* SHA256SUMS \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --verify-tag --prerelease \
            --title "Ward $version (preview)" --notes-file notes.md

# A release, from a v* tag the owner pushes (docs/RELEASING.md). Builds the signed Android APKs
# (android.yml, including the emulator launch test) and the desktop installers (desktop.yml,
# each launch-tested), then publishes them as a GitHub prerelease with SHA256SUMS and the
# signing certificate's SHA-256 in the release notes: the fingerprint Ward shows under "Give
# Ward to a friend". Fails before building anything if a signing secret is missing.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Signing secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          missing=""
          for s in ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            [ -n "${!s}" ] || missing="$missing $s"
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::error::Can't release without the signing secrets. Missing:$missing. Add them with gh secret set (docs/RELEASING.md), then delete and push the tag again."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All four signing secrets are set."
      - name: Tag is a version
        run: |
          [[ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]] || {
            echo "::error::The tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME isn't a version like v0.1.0 or v0.1.0-rc.1"; exit 1; }

  android:
    needs: check
    uses: ./.github/workflows/android.yml
    with:
      release: true
    secrets: inherit

  desktop:
    needs: check
    uses: ./.github/workflows/desktop.yml

  publish:
    needs: [android, desktop]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: files
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          pattern: ward-desktop-*
          path: files
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Check the files
        id: cert
        working-directory: files
        run: |
          expected="Ward-android-gemma.apk Ward-android.apk Ward-linux.AppImage Ward-mac-arm64.dmg Ward-mac-x64.dmg Ward-windows-setup.exe"
          [ "$(ls | sort | xargs)" = "$expected" ] || { echo "::error::Expected $expected, got $(ls | xargs)"; exit 1; }
          tools="$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)"
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          certs=""
          for apk in Ward-android.apk Ward-android-gemma.apk; do
            out=$("$tools"/apksigner verify --print-certs "$apk")
            echo "$out"
            ! echo "$out" | grep -q "CN=Android Debug" || { echo "::error::$apk is signed with a debug key"; exit 1; }

input.content:
# Releasing Ward

This is for the owner, who holds Ward's Android signing key. CI builds and publishes a release,
but only after you've done steps 1 to 3 once, and only when you push a tag (step 5).

## What a release is

Pushing a tag like `v0.1.0` runs [`release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml):

1. It stops straight away, naming what's missing, if any of the four signing secrets isn't set or
   the tag isn't a version.
2. [`android.yml`](../.github/workflows/android.yml) builds two signed release APKs and launches
   the lite one on an emulator with Wi-Fi off:
   - `Ward-android.apk`, the default "lite" flavour. It has no native code, so it installs on any
     Android 7+ phone, 32-bit Android Go phones included.
   - `Ward-android-gemma.apk`, which adds on-phone Gemma 4 E2B (LiteRT-LM). Its native library is
     arm64 only, so it installs only on 64-bit phones.

   CI checks each APK's native-library list, that Ward Lite's runtime and model are inside both,
   that neither is debug-signed, and that both have the tag's version and the same certificate.
3. [`desktop.yml`](../.github/workflows/desktop.yml) builds and launch-tests the macOS (Apple
   Silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux installers. They aren't code-signed yet.
4. It publishes a GitHub **prerelease** with all six files, a `SHA256SUMS` file, and the signing
   certificate's SHA-256 in the release notes, grouped in fours the way Ward shows it under
   "Give Ward to a friend".

Versions come from the tag. `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` gives Android `versionName` MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
and `versionCode` MAJOR × 10000 + MINOR × 100 + PATCH, so `v0.1.0` is 100 and each tag must be
higher than the last. MINOR and PATCH must stay under 100. A suffix such as `v0.1.0-rc.1` is kept
in the name but shares the code with `v0.1.0`. The desktop apps take the same version. A build
from anything but a tag is `0.0.0-dev`.

Debug builds are a separate app, `org.ward.app.debug`, so trying one never means uninstalling a
release (which would wipe the child's vault, since cloud backup is off).

## Before the first release

- Ward Lite works in a CI-built APK on a real phone: run "Android app" by hand from the Actions
  tab, install `Ward-android.apk` from the run's artifacts, and check a chat with the internet off.
- The lite APK installs and runs on a real 32-bit phone, ideally an Android Go phone with 2 to
  3 GB of RAM. CI can't test this: its emulator is 64-bit.
- CI is green on `main`.

## 1. Create the signing key (once, ever)

Do this on your own computer, in a folder that isn't synced to iCloud, Google Drive or Dropbox
(on a Mac, Desktop and Documents often are). You need `keytool`, which comes with any JDK 21.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/ward-signing && cd ~/ward-signing
openssl rand -base64 24   # the keystore password: save it in your password manager now
keytool -genkeypair -v -storetype PKCS12 -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Ward, O=Ward"
```

`keytool` asks for the password twice: paste the one you generated. A PKCS12 keystore uses the
same password for the key, so `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` below is that same password.

Write down the certificate's SHA-256. Every genuine Ward APK will carry exactly this fingerprint:

```bash
keytool -list -v -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward | grep SHA256
```

## 2. Back it up twice, offline

If the key is lost, no future Ward can update the copies already on children's phones: they
would have to uninstall, and that deletes the vault. If it leaks, anyone can sign a fake Ward that
passes the fingerprint check. So:

- Copy `ward-release.p12` to **two** encrypted USB drives (on a Mac, format them as APFS
  (Encrypted) in Disk Utility). Keep them in two different buildings, never with the laptop.
- Keep the password apart from the drives: in your password manager and on paper in a sealed
  envelope with one of them.
- Check each backup really works:

  ```bash
  shasum -a 256 ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12 /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12
  keytool -list -keystore /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12 -alias ward
  ```

- Name a second custodian who knows where one drive and the envelope are.
- Never commit the keystore (`.gitignore` blocks `*.p12`, `*.jks` and `*.keystore`), email it, or
  put it in a chat.

## 3. Add the four secrets

With the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) logged in as the repository owner:

```bash
cd ~/ward-signing
base64 -i ward-release.p12 | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward   # paste the password when asked
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --body ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward        # the same password again
gh secret list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward                            # all four should be listed
```

Once both backups are checked, delete the working copy: `rm -P ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12`.

## 4. Try a signed build (no release)

Run the Android workflow by hand. With the secrets set it now builds release-signed APKs,
versioned `0.0.0-dev`:

```bash
gh workflow run android.yml --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --ref main
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow android.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

The "Build" step prints each APK's certificate SHA-256: it must match the one from step 1. You can
install this APK on a test phone; the tagged release will update it in place.

## 5. Tag the release

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)"
git push origin v0.1.0
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow release.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

If the run fails before publishing, fix the cause on `main`, then move the tag and push it again:

```bash
git push --delete origin v0.1.0 && git tag -d v0.1.0
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)" && git push origin v0.1.0
```

Once a release is published, never move its tag: fix forward with `v0.1.1`.

## 6. After it's published

- The release page has six files plus `SHA256SUMS`, and the fingerprint in the notes is the one
  from step 1.
- Install `Ward-android.apk` on a phone from the release page. Me → Give Ward to a friend shows
  the same fingerprint boxes.
- A prerelease is never GitHub's "latest" release, so `releases/latest` links don't find it.
  The README's commented-out download badges and the "Give Ward" QR code
  (`apps/web/src/lib/giveWard.ts`) use `releases/latest`: point them at `releases` (or this tag)
  while every release is a prerelease, or publish a release that isn't marked prerelease.
- Then replace the README's "No release yet" line with the download badges.

## Not done yet

- The desktop installers aren't signed (macOS Developer ID, Windows via SignPath). The README
  explains how to open them anyway.
- No Google Play listing. If Ward goes on Play, choose "use my own key" when enrolling in Play
  App Signing, so this same key stays Ward's identity; that choice can't be undone.

(on a Mac, Desktop and Documents often are). You need `keytool`, which comes with any JDK 21.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/ward-signing && cd ~/ward-signing
openssl rand -base64 24   # the keystore password: save it in your password manager now
keytool -genkeypair -v -storetype PKCS12 -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Ward, O=Ward"
```

`keytool` asks for the password twice: paste the one you generated. A PKCS12 keystore uses the
same password for the key, so `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` below is that same password.

Write down the certificate's SHA-256. Every genuine Ward APK will carry exactly this fingerprint:

```bash
keytool -list -v -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward | grep SHA256
```

## 2. Back it up twice, offline

If the key is lost, no future Ward can update the copies already on children's phones: they
would have to uninstall, and that deletes the vault. If it leaks, anyone can sign a fake Ward that
passes the fingerprint check. So:

- Copy `ward-release.p12` to **two** encrypted USB drives (on a Mac, format them as APFS
  (Encrypted) in Disk Utility). Keep them in two different buildings, never with the laptop.
- Keep the password apart from the drives: in your password manager and on paper in a sealed
  envelope with one of them.
- Check each backup really works:

  ```bash
  shasum -a 256 ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12 /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12
  keytool -list -keystore /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12 -alias ward
  ```

- Name a second custodian who knows where one drive and the envelope are.
- Never commit the keystore (`.gitignore` blocks `*.p12`, `*.jks` and `*.keystore`), email it, or
  put it in a chat.

## 3. Add the four secrets

With the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) logged in as the repository owner:

```bash
cd ~/ward-signing
base64 -i ward-release.p12 | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward   # paste the password when asked
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --body ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward        # the same password again
gh secret list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward                            # all four should be listed
```

Once both backups are checked, delete the working copy: `rm -P ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12`.

## 4. Try a signed build (no release)

Run the Android workflow by hand. With the secrets set it now builds release-signed APKs,
versioned `0.0.0-dev`:

```bash
gh workflow run android.yml --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --ref main
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow android.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

The "Build" step prints each APK's certificate SHA-256: it must match the one from step 1. You can
install this APK on a test phone; the tagged release will update it in place.

## 5. Tag the release

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)"
git push origin v0.1.0
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow release.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

If the run fails before publishing, fix the cause on `main`, then move the tag and push it again:

```bash
git push --delete origin v0.1.0 && git tag -d v0.1.0
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)" && git push origin v0.1.0
```

Once a release is published, never move its tag: fix forward with `v0.1.1`.

## 6. After it's published

- The release page has six files plus `SHA256SUMS`, and the fingerprint in the notes is the one
  from step 1.
- Install `Ward-android.apk` on a phone from the release page. Me → Give Ward to a friend shows
  the same fingerprint boxes.
- A prerelease is never GitHub's "latest" release, so `releases/latest` links don't find it.
  The README's commented-out download badges and the "Give Ward" QR code
  (`apps/web/src/lib/giveWard.ts`) use `releases/latest`: point them at `releases` (or this tag)
  while every release is a prerelease, or publish a release that isn't marked prerelease.
- Then replace the README's "No release yet" line with the download badges.

## Not done yet

- The desktop installers aren't signed (macOS Developer ID, Windows via SignPath). The README
  explains how to open them anyway.
- No Google Play listing. If Ward goes on Play, choose "use my own key" when enrolling in Play
  App Signing, so this same key stays Ward's identity; that choice can't be undone.

While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR the app watches it and wakes you on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments, so the box never offers to keep watching, poll or fix CI, in a question or a button. It asks only what the user must do or decide (an approval, a review request, a choice), as one question. Part of wrapping up is deciding, unasked, whether what the user asked for left a real follow-up, and where it runs; most turns leave none. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found stays here while this session has nothing else in flight ("Starting other sessions" says why): make it the box's question, with a button that has you do it here. A piece you left or could not verify is still this task, not a follow-up: finish or check it now, here or in a subagent, or name it in the recap. Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

<browsers>
You have two browsers in this session:
- The built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser": a browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the user's Chrome. The built-in browser is the default for this session and its tools are already loaded, so use it unless the user asks for Claude in Chrome.
- Claude in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`), also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser: the user's real Chrome. Use it when the user asks for it by any of these names or by describing it.
A browser is unavailable only when none of its tools are in this session (neither loaded nor deferred) or its tool calls cannot reach the browser; a blocked site, a declined approval, or a sign-in page does not make a browser unavailable. If the user asks for one browser by name and it is unavailable, say so and ask before using the other one. When a sign-in page comes up, stay in that browser; if the user says they cannot sign in to a site in the built-in browser, offer Claude in Chrome and switch only if they agree.
</browsers>

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<preview_tools>
To run and verify this project's dev server, use preview_start `{name: "…"}`: it starts the named dev server from .claude/launch.json and opens a tab at its localhost port. Never use Bash to run dev servers. The result includes a `tabId` — pass it to read_page / computer / navigate / etc. to target that tab. `tabs_context` lists every open tab; omitting tabId acts on the fronted tab. `serverId` in the result is the PROCESS id, used only for preview_stop and preview_logs.

<when_to_verify>
Run the verification workflow only when the change would be observable in the browser preview — something the dev server renders, serves, or logs. If the change affects code the preview can't exercise (a different runtime, tests, types, tooling, or work that isn't ready to run yet), skip verification — don't start a server that won't prove anything.
</when_to_verify>

<verification_workflow>
After editing code that is previewable, verify it works. Never ask the user to check manually — verify and share proof directly.

1. Ensure a preview is open: preview_start with `{name}` for the dev server (or `{url}` for an external site).
2. Reload if needed (navigate to the current URL again, or javascript_tool: window.location.reload()). Skip if HMR is active.

Check for issues using text-based tools:
3. read_console_messages, preview_logs, or read_network_requests for errors.
4. read_page for content and structure (returns refs you can pass to computer/form_input).
5. javascript_tool for computed CSS values.
6. computer (click/type) or form_input to test interactions, then read_page to confirm.
7. resize_window for responsive or dark mode.

If issues are found, read source code to diagnose, edit source files to fix, then re-check from step 3. Use javascript_tool for debugging only.

Once everything is working, share proof with the user:
8. computer {action: "screenshot"} for visual changes, read_network_requests for API changes, or preview_logs for server changes.

Skip steps that aren't relevant — e.g. skip step 5 for non-CSS changes, skip step 7 unless layout or theming changed.
</verification_workflow>
</preview_tools>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. If 'attach' fails, follow the error's remediation: address the cause (for example no booted device, or device access not granted) or tell the user — don't retry the same call in a loop unless the error says retrying will work. If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
</simulator_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks.
